title: W-5: the approval prompt can be spoofed by whitespace layout
description: Source: the consolidated pre-public security review (opum-doc, 2026-10-30), reviewed at b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d; tracked under ODOC-552 and parent WCLI-95. Report id: W-5 (medium), sec-b F3. escapeForDisplay leaves ordinary spaces and NBSP, a profile may declare many long headers, and url and method print before them, so padded header values can scroll the real destination off screen and render a benign url line. No test covers prompt length or wrapping. Files: src/domain/display.ts, src/domain/profile.ts limits, src/adapters/terminal-consent.ts.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The [y/N] line repeats the method and destination host with the header count
The number and length of displayed headers are capped
Runs of whitespace and NBSP in displayed values are escaped
Tests cover prompt length and wrapping, including the padded-header spoof
Whether to require typing the host instead of y is decided and recorded

implementationNotes: Landed: opum-ai/ward-cli#233 (squash f0a1ef5, 2026-11-01). Opus rounds: 38ee43c REQUEST_CHANGES (host capped at 120 on the answer line kept the left end, hiding a registrable suffix), ebedff5 APPROVE. Measured by the leader: diff exactly 3 files, terminal-consent tests 35 of 35, restoring the 120 cap turns exactly the long-host test red, dropping Default_Ignorable_Code_Point or U+2800 turns the blank test red, dropping the fit check goes red. AC5 decided under DEC-255: keep the y/N prompt and do not require typing the host, because the answer line now shows the whole host. Residual LOWs, not fixed: the backslash is not escaped so escaping is not injective, which cannot forge a host because the trusted answer line cannot carry a backslash; headers are shown first by name so the declaration order picks which 8 show (the line now says the full set is declared in the manifest). Follow-up: WCLI-128.
